1.why: All eight screens are static single-column cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up overlays; the only extra panel is a passive Logs box.

2.why: Each screen has a large bold dark-blue heading and one filled primary button (e.g. 'Request reset instructions', 'Verify and sign in'), though the dark Logs panel competes visually and secondary buttons sit at equal size beside primary ones.

3.why: Only one task with 1-2 fields appears per screen, so the needed field is quickly found, but the technical Logs panel and the long hex token add clutter that can slow a user down.

4.why: The flow requires the user to locate a 64-character token in a Logs panel and a six-digit MFA code and transfer them into fields, plus remember the 12-character password rules across two steps.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password manager hint, autofill affordance, show-password toggle, or copy-token button is visible anywhere in the eight screens.

6.why: Nothing is saved or highlighted for recognition — the token and code must be read from raw log text, and no masked email, saved account, or previously used device indicator is shown.

7.why: Instructions are one or two short plain-language sentences per screen in a readable size, though phrases like 'simulated recovery link', 'reset token', and 'Mock MFA delivery' are jargon.

8.why: No error state is shown in any screenshot; only a neutral confirmation ('If an account can be recovered, reset instructions have been prepared') appears, so problem-plus-fix messaging is not evidenced.

9.why: The password rule 'Use 12 or more characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and symbol' and a pre-filled email placeholder give partial guidance, but no concrete sample password or code format example is provided.

10.why: Password and code steps are labelled clearly, but there is no face/biometric or alternative sign-in option offered, and the difference between 'Request reset instructions', 'Enter a reset token' and 'Use simulated recovery link' on step 2 is unclear.

11.why: Each screen presents at most two or three buttons and one or two fields, so choice load stays low, with step 2 showing the maximum of three actions.

12.why: Green confirmation banner after the request, and explicit 'Conditions accepted' screen stating the reset and acceptance were recorded, communicate outcomes, though intermediate steps give no progress indicator (e.g. step 3 of 6).

13.why: The only help content is the static 'Stay safe' anti-phishing note and the password rule line; there are no tooltips, contextual tips, or help links on the token, MFA, or privacy steps.

14.why: A 'Back' button on the token screen and 'Return to recovery start' at the end allow retrying, but most screens (new password, MFA code, privacy) offer no back, cancel, or resend-code option.

15.why: Every screen reuses the same header, white rounded card, bold heading, label-above-input pattern, teal primary button, and bottom Logs panel.
